newsitem.title: UK: Newcastle United float valued at 193 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Newcastle United float valued at 193 mln stg.

text.p: British premier league soccer club Newcastle United Plc said on Friday that its stock market flotation valued it at 193 million pounds ($307.4 million).

The offering of 40 milion new shares in the club was priced at 135 pence per share and will raise 54 million pounds gross of new funds, a statement from Newcastles's investment bank NatWest Markets said.

The NatWest statement said the offer was priced at the top of the indicative range, set last month at between 120 and 135 pence per share, and would raise 54 million pounds for the club, including charges. It said indications of interest under the offer to investment institutions "significantly exceed the amount of the offer."

Despite this, NatWest said that the retail offer, to private individuals, was being increased to 15 percent of the total offer from 10 percent after it had been oversubscribed by approximately seven times. The statement said that full details of the allocation of shares wouod be announced on March 24.

Press reports this week had said institutional support for the flotation of Newcastle United, the latest in a growing number of soccer clubs to seek a stock market quote, might have waned after the club was knocked out of the UEFA Cup by Monaco of the French league in a quarter-final on Tuesday and amid a general weakening of shares in soccer club shares, which soared in London last year on a sharp rise in revenues from television broadcasting and an increase in interest in the game itself.

Newcastle United, backed by millionaire property developer Sir John Hall who intends to remain chairman of the soccer club but will not be a director of the floated parent company, currently stand fourth in the English soccer premier league. But the team is nine points adrift of leaders Manchester United Plc, the country's largest stock market-quoted soccer club and one which has provided the model for clubs looking to build both on the pitch, and off it though commercial enterprises such as sale of club merchandise such as replica kit.
